subject: LumosHealth RFP — SLO evidence onboarding & measurement plan
messages:
From: Marcus Dunne <mdunne@lumoshealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@lumoshealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: LumosHealth SLO questionnaire and evidence request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking LumosHealth's RFP. We're walking through the SLO/SLA section and need Redwood's concrete measurement methodology and representative evidence so our procurement and engineering teams can evaluate claims around availability and latency. Key items we'd like in the next 5 business days: 

- A short doc describing how you measure availability (probe types, cadence, regional coverage, windowing).
- Latency percentiles you compute (p50/p95/p99) and how you derive them from sampling vs full telemetry.
- Example raw output for a 30-day window (CSV or JSON) showing sample records and the aggregation used to compute p99.
- The service credit matrix and how incidents map to credits (including partial-region events).
- Any dependencies on synthetic probes vs production-sampled traffic.

We're attaching the RFP SLO worksheet as a starting point (Lumos_SLO_Questionnaire.xlsx). Can you confirm the format you prefer for the telemetry sample and whether Redwood will provide an ingestion/readme for the files? Also, if there's an internal contact for security to receive telemetry hashes/evidence, please include them.

Appreciate it — Marcus
Marcus Dunne
Head of Procurement, LumosHealth
Marcus.Dunne@lumoshealth.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Dunne <mdunne@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: LumosHealth SLO questionnaire and evidence request

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear list.

We can absolutely provide the materials you asked for. Attached to this reply is a concise evidence onboarding packet (Redwood_SLO_Evidence_Plan.pdf) and a short README that describes the telemetry sample format (telemetry_sample_readme.txt). High-level answers:

- Availability measurement: we use both production-sampled request telemetry (1% by default) and active synthetic probes (per-region, 1-minute cadence) to detect and attribute partial-region degradations. Measurement windows are rolling 30-day and calendar-month windows depending on contract preference.
- Latency: we compute p50/p95/p99 on request-level latencies using weighted regional aggregation; by default we compute percentiles on raw sampled requests and use Jackknife resampling to estimate percentile stability when sample sizes are small.
- Telemetry sample: we'll provide a single JSONL file with anonymized request records and an aggregation script (see README). If you prefer CSV, we can export that as well.
- Service credits: included in the attached CSV (redwood_service_credit_matrix.csv). Credits escalate by severity and effective regionally-weighted downtime.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I'll share the sample JSONL and a Drive link tomorrow.
2) Lauren, can you prepare the anonymized 30-day sample and the aggregation script?
3) Aditya, please draft a short note about how quantization/VM restarts are excluded from customer-facing measurements (i.e., internal infra maintenance windows).

If Lumos wants a short walkthrough (30 min) of the evidence package we can schedule for later this week.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_SLO_Evidence_Plan.pdf (PDF), telemetry_sample_readme.txt (text)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: LumosHealth SLO questionnaire — actions

Folks — forwarding Lumos' SLO worksheet and our reply. Action items below (we should keep this tight since procurement asked for material within 5 biz days):

- Lauren: Produce an anonymized 30-day JSONL sample (1% sampled requests + synthetic probe records). Include fields: timestamp, region, endpoint, latency_ms, request_id (hashed), probe_flag. Add a README snippet showing how we compute p99 across weighted regions. Delivery target: EOD tomorrow.
- Aditya: Draft the short exclusion/attribution note for infrastructure maintenance, autoscaler spikes, and model-variant fallbacks; include where in the telemetry we mark a request as fallback-handled. Also review the service credit CSV and ensure the credit tiers map to our current SLAs. Delivery target: EOD tomorrow.
- I will assemble the Drive package and create a link to send to Lumos.

Keep the sample anonymized — no PII, no customer identifiers. Use synthetic UUIDs for request_id and scramble timestamps by up to ±30s for added safety.

Thanks — Soojin
From: Marcus Dunne <mdunne@lumoshealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@lumoshealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumosHealth SLO questionnaire and evidence request

Soojin — this looks good. A couple clarifying points before we ingest the sample: 

1) For the 30-day window you propose, do you compute p99 on rolling 30-day aggregates or on calendar months for invoicing/credit triggers? We need the latter for our finance team (calendar months).
2) For region weighting: can you supply both weighted and unweighted p99 so we can reconcile locally?
3) On the sample format: we prefer CSV for quick ingestion but JSONL is fine if you include a column mapping.
4) Security: add our security contact (sec-ops@lumoshealth.com) to the thread if you will provide hashes/manifest for evidence.

One more ask: can you include a small example showing how a partial-region incident maps to the service credit calculation? A one-page worked example would be ideal.

Thanks,
Marcus

--
Marcus Dunne
Head of Procurement, LumosHealth
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Dunne <mdunne@lumoshealth.com>, procurements@lumoshealth.com, sec-ops@lumoshealth.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: LumosHealth SLO questionnaire and evidence request

Marcus — thanks, and good points. See answers below and links to the sample artifacts.

- Windowing: we support both rolling 30-day and calendar-month measurement. For invoicing/credits we will use calendar-month by default; the sample includes both rolling and calendar calculations so your finance team can reconcile.
- Weighted vs unweighted: sample package includes both. We compute weighted percentiles by calculating percentiles per-region then combining via traffic-weighted interpolation; the package includes a small notebook demonstrating interpolation steps.
- Format: attached CSV export (sample_30d_anonymized.csv) and the original JSONL. README maps fields and provides a small aggregation script (agg_example.py).
- Security: included sec-ops@lumoshealth.com on this reply. For evidence integrity we publish a SHA256 manifest of delivered files and an HMAC-signed delivery token in the Drive package.

Worked example (summary):
- Event: 2026-10-23 03:12 UTC — increased p99 observed in us-west region for 47 minutes; synthetic probe failure rate in us-west = 18%, production-sampled error rate = 9%. Regional weighting = 18% of global traffic. 
- Attribution: us-west partial degradation flagged; global p99 rose from 210ms to 460ms during window. Using our credit matrix, this maps to a Level 2 partial-region incident and triggers a 6% service credit for that calendar-day applied pro rata on monthly invoice. CSV example in redwood_service_credit_matrix.csv and an annotated worked example in the Drive notebook.

Links and artifacts (read-only):
- Evidence package: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodEvidencePack
- Sample CSV: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cSampleCSV
- Aggregation notebook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cNotebook

Attachments delivered in email: redwood_service_credit_matrix.csv, sample_30d_anonymized.csv, agg_example.py.

If Lumos would like, we can run a 30-minute walkthrough next Tue/Thu (please propose a slot) and I can include our reliability engineer to answer deep telemetry questions.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
